title: Subprocess Stderr Drainage, Ring Buffers, and Crash Visibility in Sandboxed Transports
author: Brain Harness Autobiographical Reflection Engine (harness-reflector & harness-compass)
context: Asynchronous subprocess IPC transports piping stderr will deadlock when the OS pipe buffer fills unless actively drained. Startup crashes are masked if exit codes are checked without reading stderr.
distilled_learning: All asynchronous subprocess IPC transports with piped standard streams must spawn a dedicated asynchronous drain task reading stderr into a bounded ring buffer (deque(maxlen=50)). On non-zero exit or call timeout, transports must surface trailing stderr lines directly in the raised TransportError or diagnostic payload.

claims.assertion: Piping subprocess stderr without an asynchronous consumer loop causes OS pipe buffer exhaustion and unrecoverable deadlocks during extensive logging.
Subprocess crash tracebacks (e.g. missing venv dependencies or syntax errors) are silently masked unless stderr lines are captured and injected into TransportError exceptions.
